column1: Nan Ferrow/0|Did Mum ever help him with the knot?|Often. She would take it away and put something else in his hands so he could stop pulling at it.|Did he realise he was getting cross?|Not immediately. Your mother usually took the knot from him before he admitted it.

Nan Ferrow/0#1|Did Mum find his advice amusing?|Sometimes. She had generally finished the knot before he finished explaining it.|I can imagine him following her around.|With great seriousness, love. She knew when to listen and when to give him another job.

Nan Ferrow/1|You let me keep the moth there?|Long enough to care for it, though I would have preferred a tin without flour in it. It eventually flew off quite well.|Was the moth badly hurt?|It recovered enough to fly straight past me when I opened the tin. You were delighted.

Nan Ferrow/1#1|I should have helped clean up.|You did, with more enthusiasm than efficiency. I was mostly pleased to see you care about the little creature.|Did you still manage to bake that day?|Not with that flour. There were other days for baking, and plenty for retelling the incident.

Nan Ferrow/2|Did it help him find his way home?|It helped him keep his bearings. He still paid attention to the paths and asked when he needed directions.|I like carrying something he used.|I am glad, love. Remember the person it belonged to without feeling you must repeat every journey he made.

royal/King Halvard/Why visit Thornwell yourself?|Do you want a welcome or obedience?|I prefer not to separate services my subjects can provide together.|A forced smile tells you very little.|It tells me they remember where authority sits. That is enough for the visit.

royal/King Halvard/Life at Cinderhold|Does anyone there tell you no?|A competent servant learns to offer a useful answer instead.|Bess still has to pay for what you drink.|Then she should value the distinction of serving her king. You are strangely determined to make generosity sound like a bill.

royal/Serjeant Bram/Following orders|Do you ever question whether an order hurts people?|My task is to carry it out. Yours is to stop confusing an audience with an inquiry into my duties.|Does the uniform decide for you?|The uniform tells you whose authority I exercise. I suggest you attend to that part.

royal/Serjeant Bram/The roadblocks|What if someone needs urgent help?|They explain themselves to the guard, who decides whether the request warrants interruption.|Why must every errand wait for the crown?|Because the crown's business takes precedence. You may find the arrangement inconvenient without altering it.

royal/Serjeant Bram/What do you write in those reports?|You know those names belong to people.|I know precisely whom I record. That is why the report is useful.|Could you leave an innocent reader out?|I record what I am ordered to record. Do not ask me to conceal something on your account.

royal/Doran/Still hunting things that do not exist?|You changed your meaning rather quickly.|A useful skill near the king. You might consider acquiring it.|Were you complaining about the search?|I was discussing its remarkable duration. Notice how much safer that sounds.

royal/Doran/You laughed at Bess|It wasn't funny for the person paying.|Then it was fortunate for me I was seated on this side of the table.|Could you choose not to laugh?|I could choose a great many things that would make my evening less comfortable.

royal/Doran/Did you search the whole town?|Why look under a cart?|Ask Tolan. He approached the task with an enthusiasm I chose not to interrupt.|Did you trouble the people living there?|We conducted the crown's search. If they found it troublesome, they were encouraged to remain patient.

royal/Tolan/Is this what being a knight means?|That sounds like making people afraid.|Then they will be careful. You could learn from the example.|Does everyone have to obey without a question?|Questions take time. His Majesty seldom enjoys waiting while we collect them.

royal/Tolan/Are you afraid of the king?|I am asking quietly.|And I am answering cautiously. Keep those two achievements together.|You watch him before every answer.|An observant habit you might imitate instead of discussing.

royal/Tolan/Are you afraid of the king?#1|Does being safe matter more than being fair?|Here, staying safe gives a man another day to consider fairness.|What if you are on the wrong side tomorrow?|Then I shall regret not noticing sooner. That is why I keep watching.

royal/Tolan/The man waiting at the roadblock|You could have treated them decently while they waited.|I could also have invited questions from Bram about why I was making friends at a closed road.|You keep giving the king's opinion instead of yours.|There is less danger in repeating the opinion that already governs the room.

visit/host/before|Did they agree to pay anything?|They treated feeding them as my duty. I still have suppliers who expect actual coin.|Could you refuse another supper?|Not without risking more than a few ingredients. That is what makes the demand so cruel.

visit/host/after|Will the missing payment hurt the tavern?|Yes. Their departure does not replace what they consumed.|Can you get back to ordinary business now?|I hope so. I would welcome a customer whose order is an agreement instead of a threat.

visit/hunter/before|What were they looking for?|They have been asking questions and searching. I would rather not supply a guess they could turn into an accusation.|Does their search make the town safer?|Not for people who worry what an officer might decide an ordinary thing means.

visit/hunter/after|Will people be relieved the search has ended?|Yes, though they will still wonder what was written in the reports.|What should I watch for on the road?|The royal party and its escort. Give yourself room and do not mistake their departure for kindness.

visit/records/before|Why ask about the histories?|They want to know whether the accounts we keep agree with the crown's preferred version.|Would you destroy an older account?|Preserving it matters. I will not pretend an account never existed because somebody finds it inconvenient.

visit/records/after|Will you keep the older accounts available?|That remains the work, with care for the people helping preserve them.|Could they come back for the books?|Possibly. Their departure is a relief, not a promise that the question has ended.

visit/supplies/before|Are they paying for the supplies?|They treat what they take as tribute. Calling it a visit makes it sound more voluntary.|What happens to your ordinary customers?|They have to manage with what remains, while we explain why the royal party came first.

visit/supplies/after|Does their leaving replace what they took?|No. We still have the shortage and the work of recovering from it.|Can people trade normally again?|More comfortably, I hope. The next demand should not be the first thing in every conversation.

visit/students/before|What questions would you have asked?|How his claims about the past compare with the records we are studying.|Why should learning about him forbid questions?|Because they want repetition of an approved answer, not an inquiry that might lead somewhere else.

visit/students/after|Can you discuss the visit more freely now?|More freely than with armed men nearby, though we still choose our listeners carefully.|Did the visit answer any of your questions?|It showed how he handles being questioned. That is an answer of a sort.

visit/neighbours/before|Are people afraid of being overheard?|Yes. Even a familiar room feels different when an officer may repeat what was said.|What do you want from the visit?|For them to leave without taking more from the people who live here.

visit/neighbours/after|Will people relax now they have gone?|Some will. Others will wait before trusting an ordinary conversation again.|Have they left much trouble behind?|Enough worried neighbours. We would like to return to concerns that belong to our own lives.
